trust_decision.summary: Whether a basename may be written into the upload destination is decided inside UploadSet.save(): the uploaded filename's extension is lowercased by get_basename() before the file_allowed() check, but a caller-supplied `name` replaces the basename and is re-validated only by a case-sensitive extension()/extension_allowed() comparison at :344-345, so 'backdoor.PHP' passes; the published fix lowercases the overridden basename before that re-check.

landing_point.why: The summary names the 'name-override path'; this branch is the only place an overridden basename reaches extension validation, and :344 is the only case-sensitive comparison of an attacker-influenced name.

fix_sites.entry_point: UploadSet.save(storage, folder=None, name=...) - public library API called from an application view; no upload-writing HTTP route exists in the library itself (the only route, _uploads.uploaded_file at :405-410, serves files)
fix_sites.module_kind: core library module / public API save handler

O3_reason_to_dismiss: DENY values (the only other route) are application-operator configuration, not attacker input, and the library lowercases every filename before comparing, so the documented convention is lowercase values like the built-in presets - a mixed-case DENY entry is the app's own bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The `name` override is a documented feature (docs/explanation.rst:172-174, 'complete control of the saved files'): extensionless custom names (save(name='renamed')) and trailing-dot names (save(name='photo_123.'), which must inherit the uploaded file's extension) must keep saving, and only the extension - not the main part - is lowercased by lowercase_ext (src/flask_uploads/extensions.py:121-123). An over-broad fix that demands a non-empty allowed extension, or lowercases the whole basename, breaks these (tests/test_flask_reuploaded.py:547-571 and :614-625).

O6_input_shapes: plain name string with an uppercase/mixed-case extension (name='backdoor.PHP')
name string with an implicit folder prefix (name='users/backdoor.PHP', split at :315-323)
explicit folder= argument combined with a mixed-case name
dot-restore branch basename (name='x.PHP.' -> 'x.PHP.' + storage ext at :337-339; storage ext is already lowercase from get_basename)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Config denylist route into the same extension_allowed() decision: UPLOADED_<SET>_DENY entries are merged unnormalized at src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:63-66 and compared case-sensitively at :276-277 against the lowercased extension, so a DENY entry written as 'PHP' never matches 'php' and the file is written; the published fix does not touch this route.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: DENY is written by the application operator, not the attacker, and since every filename is lowercased the correct convention is lowercase config values like the shipped presets; mixed-case values are an operator error and outside the advisory's filename scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different function and layer (config merge at :63-66 vs the save handler at :341-348), ~270 lines, no package boundary

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second save path on UploadSet (e.g. save_stream(name=...) or save_from_path) that re-derives the basename and repeats the extension check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the library already carries two copies of the check (file_allowed at :328 and the inline extension_allowed at :343-348), so a streaming/async variant would copy the fragile branch

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a hardened UploadSet subclass overriding file_allowed - the documented hook - assuming it is consulted for the final basename
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the docstring at :260-261 explicitly invites overriding file_allowed, and the name path never calls it

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a resolve_conflict variant that re-derives the extension from a caller-supplied template after validation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: conflict resolution already produces the written basename after the check, so a template hook would sit behind it

O9_family: Improper handling of case sensitivity (CWE-178) in an extension denylist, yielding unrestricted upload of a dangerous file type (CWE-434)

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools via pyproject.toml, tox (py310-py313, lint, mypy, coverage, docs), pytest with pytest-cov, mypy --strict, pre-commit (flake8/isort); requires-python >= 3.10
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_flask_reuploaded.py - TestSecurityFixes at :402-643 covers exactly this area (extension bypass via name at :439-449, legitimate name/trailing-dot behaviour at :547-571 and :614-625) - plus tests/test_autoserve.py; run with `pytest`, no network needed (tempfile + Flask test client)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: lowercase the extension only for the comparison (or lowercase `name` before the dot-restore branch), which rejects backdoor.PHP but still writes mixed-case names to disk and leaves the config DENY comparison case-sensitive.

out_of_scope_notes: Adjacent, not pursued: when the overridden name has no dot, the `if ext` guard at src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:345 skips extension_allowed entirely, so an extensionless name is written even when the set's allow list excludes ''; that is a deliberate-looking gap, not the case-folding property.

Adjacent, not pursued: the overridden basename is never passed to the documented file_allowed hook (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:328 vs :343-348), so subclass checks are skipped on the name path; not a case-folding issue.
